description: §39.2 / §39.4 (S479) — `<schema>` column type names and constraint words are case-insensitive, lowercase canonical: `id: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`, `email: Text Not Null Unique`, `REAL DEFAULT(0)`, `INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)` declare exactly what their lowercase spellings declare. The whole E-SCHEMA-* family stays silent, and the uppercase `PRIMARY KEY` is the table's key (no W-SCHEMA-001).
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S479 "⭐ RULED — the rest of S478 hand-off §3.B, PA recs adopted" item 3 (gap g-boot-schema-type-case-s478)
rationale: §39.2: "The `column-type` names (§39.4) and the words of a `column-constraint` — `primary`, `key`, `not`, `null`, `unique`, `default`, `references`, `rename`, `from` — SHALL be matched case-insensitively; the lowercase spelling is canonical." §39.4: "The type names are matched case-insensitively, lowercase canonical". Newly-accepting on the bootstrap (it reported `id: INTEGER` as E-SCHEMA-004 and refused `PRIMARY KEY` by name); impl#1 already lowercases.
